Skeptical evidence review, round 1
29 September 2026. Internal academic review of the conditional mechanism report and its evidence
companion, without public transactions or state simulations. This review reuses earlier bridge studies:
the present recalculation is an independent check of saved records, not an independent investigator or a
second independent blockchain data provider. Origin/Morpho analysis was not reopened. The main paper
was not edited.
Assessment
The paper supports a coherent conditional financing architecture and contains substantial evidence of
particular destination-chain actions. It does not establish that the complete proposed source-to-pDAI
route is executable in the pinned deployed state, or that such a route has established a durable dollar
price. The main report generally states these distinctions correctly. Its most important residual risk is
that readers mistake a large catalogue of true local observations for evidence connecting those
observations into the proposed system.
The strongest positive evidence is the token-specific GRT mint: a mint call, zero-address token event,
gateway event and exact supply increase agree. The strongest contrary evidence to an already
configured Portal route is the stated zero unbacked caps, additionally constrained by actual reserve cash
and supply limits. The strongest source-provenance warning is that the ARB execution's recorded source
blocks and timestamp are not plausible chronology. None of these facts disproves every future or
separately specified architecture.
Representative checks performed
The reviewed main-paper and evidence-companion file hashes, raw input hashes, and calculated results
are saved in artifacts/pulsechain-skeptic-evidence-round1-20260929/. These identify the versions reviewed
even if the papers change after round 1. The endpoint remains block 27,659,393, hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275.

No sampled contradiction was found. This review did not independently replay all 78 traces, inspect
every token's implementation, validate every receipt against a header receipt root, or repeat the entire
audit against another archival node. It must not be cited as having done those things.
Strongest evidence supporting the limited thesis
Destination issuance is demonstrated, rather than inferred from a function name. ARB and GRT have
actual destination mint histories, so a universal claim that L1 delivery always requires existing L1
token escrow is false for these integrations. GRT's executed amount is tied to its specific allowance,
not an assumed infinite mint facility.
1. 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 362

The historical reverse-gateway accounting is coherent: custody of a transferable invested receipt
can support a destination representation while the underlying remains invested. It is not necessary
to withdraw every underlying asset before transferring ownership of its receipt claim.
Exact local wrappers and matching pools, actual wrapper sales, an existing eUSD issuer and actual
Curve trades establish meaningful destination components. They make a composition hypothesis
worth examining, while not proving the components were joined by the claimed funding flow.
Specific governance and ownership events rebut the idea that nothing changed after the fork. The
paper also correctly distinguishes an executed upgrade, a queued proposal, module ownership and
human attribution.
The AMM example correctly distinguishes marginal price from the execution value of a finite sale.
Under its assumptions, finite purchasing input can move the specified price without buying all pDAI
supply.
Strongest objections to the stronger interpretation
Destination acceptance is not source collateral verification. An L1 trace proves which accepted
call executed. It does not independently prove a real source lock or burn, the source application's
balance sheet, uniqueness of the claim, or economic redemption. With assumed administrative control of
the acceptance path, successful destination execution is particularly unsuitable as independent
corroboration of what that same path asserted. The ARB metadata makes this limitation concrete. GRT is
a strong destination example without being evidence of source investment remaining locked.
The fork supplies L1 state, not every operating L2 database. The paper now states this. Its
operating pARB premise is permissible in a theoretical model, but it cannot simultaneously be counted
as a retrospective finding. Repository availability before the fork also differs from deployed code and
functioning cross-chain configuration at the fork.
Exact-token permissions prevent generalization. ARB's reverse bridge, GRT's limited issuer
permission and LPT's external-minter branch are different. They do not issue the named existing
stablecoins or Aave receipts. The named addresses' standard-gateway routes support an escrow
interpretation. A newly created representation may be a perfectly coherent asset while still being
unacceptable to the existing pool or issuer at issue.
The scenario assumes the economically decisive links. Source operation, usable assets, the
required authority, compatible integration and actual purchasing liquidity are explicit premises. Once
adequate financing and an executable market route are assumed, the existence of a purchasable
quantity is unsurprising. The conditional paper demonstrates compatibility of selected accounting
models, not discovery of endogenous funding or proof that nominal copied collateral commands the
required market value. The finite AMM example is a local price theorem with exogenous PLS purchasing
power; it is not a proof that the bridge generates that purchasing power.
Observations of disconnected steps are not a complete cash-flow record. A GRT mint, an mUSD
swap, a debt repayment and a governance action by different addresses and dates cannot be composed
retrospectively without tracing the assets, quantities, liabilities and intervening changes. Proposal
execution does not establish that all necessary configuration changed; historical message emission does
not establish counterpart execution. A queued inherited proposal need not be a new plan.
A price intervention does not establish a durable dollar commitment. A stated external PLS
reference is a defensible measurement convention, but it adds an external valuation dependency. Cash
needed for future sales, changing PLS value, creditor withdrawals and refinancing remains finite. Aave
settlement cash backs aT okens; it is not independent free intervention capital. No reviewed record
establishes an operational intervention rule, complete balance sheet or ability to sustain specified selling
and redemption conditions.

observed links

destination asset?
Source contract and state identifiers,
an existing deposit/lock or burn
record, corresponding message

reconciliation; absence of a public RPC
may require another verifiable source
record
3 Which exact destination token and
spending route is claimed?
Address-level identity, effective
issuance authority, current
implementation, actual required
configuration and liquidity at a
common time; registration alone is
insufficient
4 Where did the purchase funds go and
what obligations remain?
Linked historical asset movements
through issuance, trading and
settlement, with source receipts, local
claims, borrowings and unbacked
principal counted once
5 What does "$1" mean and for how
long?
Specified external reference, sale
quantity, fees, horizon and seller/
redemption scenario, plus a funded
balance-sheet analysis; no finite test
proves unlimited duration under
arbitrary flows
6 What control claim is necessary? Roles and successful authorized
actions at the relevant time; human
identity only if separately evidenced
and needed for the claim
7 Can another researcher reproduce the
review?
Frozen document version, scripts,
manifests, exact query inputs, raw
evidence access and archival-provider
details; an independent node or
cryptographic inclusion checks where
stronger authenticity is asserted
For a theoretical existence claim, the missing source and integration facts can remain explicit
assumptions. For an actual-history claim they must become observations. Those are different proof
obligations; more examples of unrelated destination mints do not substitute for the missing link in either
case.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 364

Snapshot and reproducibility limits
The negative findings are bounded by selected addresses, signatures, intervals and the provider's
returned history. T wenty successful partitions corroborate query consistency, not completeness of every
possible call or nonstandard state change. Endpoint equality does not exclude intervening upgrades; the
paper's recorded temporary gateway upgrade is a useful counterexample. Its disclosed pre-fork control-
query gap must remain disclosed.
Hash matching detects changes relative to the saved manifests. A manifest created from the same RPC
response does not independently authenticate the response. Traces are node-derived execution
descriptions, while receipt logs and state are separately structured commitments; no independent
commitment validation was performed in this round. Explorer verification is useful but is not this review's
own source-to-runtime compilation check.
The raw evidence is intentionally under ignored artifacts. A checkout alone therefore does not reproduce
the paper's exact archived observations unless the raw batches are also provided or all historical
endpoints remain available. Publication should make the frozen evidence bundle available with its
existing hashes and retain data-provider limitations. This is a reproducibility condition, not a reason to
discard the positive transaction evidence.
Confidence judgments for cross-review comparison
These are subjective epistemic ranges about the propositions and the evidence presented, not
probabilities of future token prices, and not statistically estimated confidence intervals. Shared
records make reviews' judgments correlated. They should not be multiplied as independent evidence.
Proposition Epistemic confidence Basis
H1: Some authorized source receipt
representation can finance a local
purchase if accepted, valued and
funded
95–99% Coherent custody/claim accounting
and ordinary financing logic; exact
concrete integrations remain
conditions
H2: This paper establishes a complete
route executable at the pinned
deployed snapshot
0–5% The paper explicitly does not establish
this; material source, permission,
configuration, settlement and
purchasing-power links remain open
H3: Validator/admin control and
nominal copied collateral alone suffice
for the target
0–1% Authority does not supply acceptance,
spendable counterpart assets or
economically independent value
H4: This paper establishes a durable
$1 under selling/redemption
0–1% No specified funded, time-bounded
stress case or complete intervention
ledger establishes that result
H5: The finite AMM existence
mathematics is valid under its stated
assumptions
99–100% Direct independent high-precision
recalculation agrees; application to
actual markets is a separate unproved
proposition
The original A/B/C framing corresponds to H1, H2 and H4 respectively. Very low H2/H4 support is not a
forecast that future implementation or price support cannot occur. It means the present report does not
establish those stronger propositions. Round 1 ends here pending the other reviews' findings.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 365
